notes: Well-studied terrestrial analog regions. Bounding boxes are approximate (drawn by Claude to contain the cited study areas) and only decide the KNOWN_ANALOG / NEW_CANDIDATE label.

regions.name: Atacama Desert
regions.why: Hyper-arid desert used for Mars life-detection and rover tests.
regions.bbox_note: Approximate: coastal range to the Andean foothills, 18-30 S.

regions.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
regions.why: Cold, dry, ice-free valleys used as a Mars polar analog.

regions.name: Iceland
regions.why: Basaltic volcanism, lava fields and glaciers; Apollo astronauts trained there.

regions.name: Hawaii (Mauna Kea / Kilauea)
regions.why: Basaltic shield volcanoes and lava tubes used for ISRU and habitat tests.

regions.name: Devon Island (Haughton crater)
regions.why: Polar desert with the Haughton impact crater; home of the Haughton-Mars Project.

regions.name: Utah (MDRS, Hanksville)
regions.why: Red sedimentary badlands around the Mars Desert Research Station.

regions.name: Rio Tinto
regions.why: Acidic, iron-rich river used as an analog for Meridiani-type environments.
regions.bbox_note: Approximate: river basin from the source to the estuary.

regions.name: Svalbard
regions.why: Arctic volcanic and permafrost sites (AMASE expeditions).

regions.name: Pilbara
regions.why: Archean stromatolites; reference for ancient biosignatures.
regions.bbox_note: Approximate: Pilbara Craton outcrop area, not the whole administrative region.

regions.name: Meteor Crater
regions.why: Well-preserved simple impact crater; Apollo crews trained there.
regions.bbox_note: Approximate: about 30 km around the crater, larger than a 32 km patch.

regions.name: Lanzarote
regions.why: Basaltic lava fields and lava tubes; ESA PANGAEA training site.

regions.name: Mojave Desert
regions.why: Arid desert used for rover field tests (JPL Mars Yard trials, Mojave volcanic fields).
regions.bbox_note: Approximate core of the desert; excludes the Colorado Desert.
